review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines reduced degree-zero Mayer–Vietoris maps (connecting map, difference map, sum map) for singular homology of two open sets. I built these on the project's own reduced singular homology (augmentation kernel) and two-open Mayer–Vietoris API. I searched Mathlib for reducedSingularHomology and MayerVietoris (case-insensitive). The only hits were the sheaf-theoretic and Grothendieck-topology Mayer–Vietoris files (Topology/Sheaves/MayerVietoris, Sites/MayerVietorisSquare, Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris). Those concern sheaf cohomology and are not the same concept as the singular-chain, augmentation-kernel construction here. I found no Mathlib reduced singular homology or singular Mayer–Vietoris to duplicate. The named maps are thin wrappers over biprod.lift, biprod.desc and kernel.lift, and they carry their own sign conventions and API (_ordinary, _naturality, _swap_eq_neg). I did not read the sibling Reduced.lean definitions in the Formal Frontier library. I judged this safe to skip, because the rubric concerns concepts already in Mathlib, and Mathlib has none here. No justified finding.
